pages.text: Push a conducting fluid across a magnetic field and it becomes the armature of a generator: the field drives current across the flow, into $(item)MHD Electrodes$() on the channel walls. No turbine, no moving parts.

Power per cubic metre is p = σu²B²k(1 − k): conductivity, speed squared, field squared. The load factor k is the share of the voltage the outside circuit takes; one half gives the most - unless the current density, j = σuB(1 − k), would arc the electrodes away.
Brine conducts a little, magma a little less but the Interior has oceans of it, and $(fluid)Stellar Plasma$() conducts ten thousand times better. The pumps limit how fast a dense fluid can be driven.
